references.text: Jesus' calling of Simon (Peter) and Andrew, as well as James and John by the Sea of Galilee, who are the first four disciples mentioned in Luke 6:14.
Matthew's list of the twelve apostles, which contains the same names as in Luke 6:14: Simon Peter, Andrew, James, John, Philip, and Bartholomew.
Mark's list of the twelve apostles, including Simon who was given the name Peter, James and John (sons of Zebedee), Andrew, Philip, and Bartholomew.
John's account of how Andrew (Simon Peter's brother) and Philip were called to follow Jesus, and how Philip found Nathanael (often identified with Bartholomew).
The list of apostles gathered in the upper room after Jesus' ascension, with the same names: Peter, John, James, Andrew, Philip, and Bartholomew.
Jesus gives Simon the name Cephas (Peter), which corresponds to Luke's note that Jesus called Simon Peter (ὃν καὶ ὠνόμασεν Πέτρον).
Mark's account of the calling of Simon and Andrew, and then James and John – the first four mentioned in the apostle lists.
